_doc: Domains (kinds of product). hue_zones are OKLCH hue ranges [lo, hi] in degrees where a primary usually works. accent_zones are for the accent when this domain is the secondary one in a mix. chroma is low | mid | high. moods are the default moods. aka are words that match a free-text brief. want works like it does in moods.json. avoid and note are prose that feed DESIGN.md Do's and Don'ts.

food-delivery.label: Food delivery and ordering
avoid: A cool blue-black base mutes the food. Keep the ground warm.
Do not make green the main color unless the brand is about health. It reads as diet food.
food-delivery.note: Warm reds, oranges and yellows raise appetite. Photography does most of the work, so the interface must step back and let the food be the brightest thing.

restaurant-cafe.label: Restaurant, cafe or bakery
avoid: Avoid neon or cold gray. The room should feel warm and a little worn in.
restaurant-cafe.note: Think of printed menus: cream paper, ink, one accent. Serifs and small rules say craft.

wellness-meditation.label: Meditation, sleep and calm apps
avoid: Do not use pure white or pure black. Both feel harsh.
Avoid red for anything but real errors. It raises alertness.
Avoid fast motion, counters that tick and loud notifications.
wellness-meditation.note: Low chroma, soft lightness steps and hues that sit back (teal, sage, dusk blue, lavender). Similar hues feel calm together. Keep one gentle warm accent for the main action.

fitness-training.label: Fitness and training
avoid: Do not use red for progress. It looks like an error.
Avoid pastel as the main color. It drains the energy.
fitness-training.note: Numbers are the product (reps, pace, streak), so type them large and tabular. Use one hot accent for effort and a cooler color for recovery.

health-medical.label: Healthcare, clinic and medical
avoid: Do not use red for non-errors. Red must keep its meaning here.
Avoid dense decoration. People may be anxious or in pain.
health-medical.note: Calm blues and teals with plenty of white space read as safe. Use large touch targets and very clear status colors, and never rely on color alone.

fintech-banking.label: Fintech, banking and payments
avoid: Blue is the default, so a plain blue blends in. Push the hue, the neutral or the type to stand out.
Do not use green and red as the only signal for gain and loss.
fintech-banking.note: Blue says trust, green says growth, a refined violet or teal stands apart. Money is shown in large tabular numerals, and everything else stays calm.

crypto-web3.label: Crypto and web3
avoid: Neon gradients on everything look like every other token site. Pick one glow and keep the rest quiet.
crypto-web3.note: Dark ground, luminous accents, mono for addresses and hashes. Trust still matters, so contrast and clear numbers stay high.

saas-productivity.label: SaaS, B2B and productivity tools
avoid: Default indigo and Inter is the look of a thousand templates. Change at least one of hue, neutral or type voice.
saas-productivity.note: People live in this UI all day. Keep chroma modest, keep the neutral carefully chosen, and spend the color on state and the single primary action.

developer-tools.label: Developer tools and infrastructure
avoid: Do not hide state in color alone. Syntax and status need shape and text too.
developer-tools.note: Dark by default, mono accents, tight spacing, fast motion. Syntax colors need their own tuned set that holds up on both grounds.

ai-assistant.label: AI assistants and generative tools
avoid: The purple-blue gradient is now a cliché for AI. Choose a warm or earthy accent to stand out.
ai-assistant.note: Conversation is the interface, so reading comfort leads: generous line height, quiet ground, one warm accent for the human touch.

analytics-bi.label: Analytics, BI and dashboards
avoid: Do not let brand color compete with data colors. Keep the chrome neutral and give charts their own palette.
analytics-bi.note: Chrome stays gray so data can carry color. Build a separate categorical palette, check it for color-blind safety, and use direct labels.

ecommerce-retail.label: E-commerce and retail
avoid: Do not use the sale color everywhere. If everything shouts, nothing converts.
Keep price and the buy button the clearest things on screen.
ecommerce-retail.note: Warm accents push action, and a calm base keeps products readable. Keep one color for price and sale, and one for the main buy button.

fashion-luxury.label: Fashion, luxury and jewelry
avoid: Too many colors reads cheap. Keep one controlled accent.
No bouncy motion and no sticker shapes.
fashion-luxury.note: Price tier shows up in restraint: low chroma, warm neutrals, one accent, lots of space, large quiet type. Use the 60-30-10 rule.

beauty-cosmetics.label: Beauty, skincare and cosmetics
avoid: Avoid default pink-for-women thinking. Use warm neutrals and let the product color speak.
beauty-cosmetics.note: Soft skin-tone neutrals, a muted rose or sage, airy type. Photos of texture and light lead.

kids-education.label: Children's products and learning
avoid: Playful is not low contrast. Keep text strongly readable.
Do not use more than four hues at once. It turns to noise.
kids-education.note: Bright, clear hues on a calm ground, big touch targets, friendly shapes and rewards for progress. Parents see the same app, so keep a calm layer for them.

education-academic.label: Universities and serious learning
avoid: Do not copy the college-sports look. Keep it sober.
education-academic.note: Deep blues, burgundies or greens, serif text for long reading, quiet motion.

travel-hospitality.label: Travel, hotels and tourism
avoid: Do not use stock-photo blue everywhere. Take colors from the destination instead.
travel-hospitality.note: Open, airy and warm. Let photography set the palette: a sea trip leans teal, a desert trip leans clay.

real-estate.label: Real estate and property
avoid: Do not use loud promo colors for listings. They cheapen big purchases.
real-estate.note: Stable, valuable and calm: deep green or navy with warm neutrals. Price and place lead, and photos are large.

legal-gov.label: Legal, government and civic
avoid: No playful shapes or motion. Clarity beats charm.
Forms must be readable at 200% zoom and by screen readers.
legal-gov.note: Serious, plain and readable. Plenty of contrast, strong focus rings, simple language, and a visible grid.

news-media.label: News, media and publishing
avoid: Do not let ads or promos use the brand accent. Keep it for the masthead and links.
news-media.note: Type does the work. A serif for text, a sans for UI, one accent for links and alerts, and rules between stories.

music-audio.label: Music, podcasts and audio
avoid: UI color must not fight the album art. Let cover colors tint the screen.
music-audio.note: Dark canvas so artwork glows. Pull accent colors from the cover. Controls are big and round and stay put.

video-photo.label: Photography, video and creative tools
avoid: Do not tint the editing canvas. Neutral gray keeps color judgments honest.
video-photo.note: Chrome recedes on a neutral dark canvas, and the work is the brightest thing. Accent only the active tool.

gaming.label: Games and entertainment
avoid: Keep HUD text readable on busy backgrounds. Use a solid plate behind small text.
gaming.note: Saturated, high-contrast and expressive. Rewards deserve rich motion, but menus stay quick.

social-community.label: Social and community apps
avoid: Do not use red for likes if red also means error. Pick a separate hue.
social-community.note: Friendly and quick. Content from people leads, so UI color stays supportive. A signature shape (the avatar, the bubble) is the identity.

hr-people.label: HR, recruiting and team tools
avoid: Avoid cold corporate gray. People data should feel human.
hr-people.note: Empathetic and balanced: a warm violet or coral with a friendly sans and soft shapes, balanced by a clear data layer.

nonprofit-impact.label: Non-profit, NGO and impact
avoid: Do not use guilt colors (heavy dark red) around donate buttons.
nonprofit-impact.note: Grounded and honest. Real photos, warm earth tones, big plain type, and one clear donate action.

sustainability-agri.label: Sustainability, agriculture and outdoors
avoid: Plain bright green looks like a template. Shift toward olive, moss or sea green, and add a soil or sun accent.
sustainability-agri.note: Natural, but not a default green. Use olive, moss, clay and sky, and let texture and photos lead.

logistics-industrial.label: Logistics, construction and industrial
avoid: Use high-visibility colors for status, and never for decoration.
Design for gloves, glare and low light: big targets and high contrast.
logistics-industrial.note: High-visibility yellow or orange against deep neutral, straight edges, and data that reads at a glance.

automotive-mobility.label: Automotive and mobility
avoid: In-car UI must work at a glance. Keep text big and contrast high.
automotive-mobility.note: Precise and premium: dark neutral, one signal color, large numerals. Use glare-safe contrast for anything seen while driving.

smart-home-iot.label: Smart home and IoT
avoid: Do not use color alone for on and off. Add icons and labels.
smart-home-iot.note: Reliable and quiet. Big toggles, clear state, and one warm color that means 'on'.

marketplace-classifieds.label: Marketplaces and classifieds
avoid: Trust badges need a distinct color from promotions.
marketplace-classifieds.note: Dense lists of photos and prices. Keep the chrome calm, show trust signals clearly, and use one color for 'verified'.

events-ticketing.label: Events, ticketing and nightlife
avoid: Do not let the hero art make the date and price hard to read.
events-ticketing.note: Poster energy: huge type, dark ground, one hot color. Date, place and price stay plain and big.

pets-family.label: Pets, family and parenting
avoid: Avoid baby-blue and pink defaults. Choose warmer, richer pairs.
pets-family.note: Soft, warm and kind. Rounded shapes and real photos. Keep a calm layer for serious tasks like health records.

religion-community.label: Faith and cultural communities
avoid: Do not use a color or symbol that has a sacred or sensitive meaning as decoration. Ask the community.
Respect right-to-left layouts and local numerals when the language needs them.
religion-community.note: Respectful and quiet. Deep green, gold, indigo or earth tones are common, but follow the community's own visual language rather than a stereotype.

creative-portfolio.label: Portfolios and creative studios
avoid: Do not use a template hero. This is the one domain where the layout itself is the brand.
creative-portfolio.note: Any hue works here, so pick a surprising one on purpose. Type and layout carry the voice.
